class="docs-prompt-preview" aria-label="Prompt preview" tabindex="0">You&#x27;re Claude Code, working in my repository.

Task
Give this repository its Muse Code project context. Run `muse init --dry-run` first; if there&#x27;s no AGENTS.md, run `muse init` and fill it with this repo&#x27;s real commands and conventions. Add .agents/memory/MEMORY.md as an index with one Markdown file per durable fact you find (deploy steps, why a workaround exists, a service&#x27;s quirks). Then show me, without writing it, a ~/.config/muse/settings.json with only what I ask for and &quot;schema_version&quot;: 1.

Read this first
Meta&#x27;s docs page &quot;Configuration and context&quot; as Markdown: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/configuration.md
It&#x27;s the source of truth for request and response shapes. The same page for people: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/configuration

Setup
- Muse Code: muse on PATH (install: curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh, or irm https://dev.meta.ai/install.ps1 | iex on Windows; check: muse --version). Its default model is muse-spark-1.2; --model picks another.
- Auth: muse reads META_API_KEY from the environment (in CI, from the secret store), else a key stored with muse auth set or a browser sign-in; not MODEL_API_KEY. Never hard-code, print or commit the key.
- Python: a plain script that runs muse through subprocess where a step needs it.

Facts to get right
- ~/.config/muse/settings.json needs &quot;schema_version&quot;: 1, or every command fails (&quot;malformed settings file&quot;; other values: &quot;unsupported settings schema version&quot;). A missing file is fine.
- Keys: permissions.default_profile, session_retention_days, show_reasoning, tui.terminal_background, agents.execution_capacity (1-64), mcp_servers, hooks, managed_hooks_path.
- From the workspace root up to .git, each level uses the first of AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .agents/AGENTS.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md. Project beats user, deeper beats shallower; project rules need a trusted workspace.
- `muse init` writes only AGENTS.md and stops if one exists (--force overwrites it).
- Memory: MEMORY.md indexes one file per topic (48 listed at most). It loads even in untrusted workspaces: no secrets or instructions in it.
- Default model muse-spark-1.2 (--model); Meta rejects --reasoning-effort none.

Starter code (Python)
import json
import pathlib

memory = pathlib.Path(&quot;.agents/memory&quot;)
memory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
topics = {&quot;deploy.md&quot;: &quot;How we ship to production and roll back&quot;}
(memory / &quot;MEMORY.md&quot;).write_text(&quot;# Memory\n&quot; + &quot;&quot;.join(f&quot;- [{f[:-3]}]({f}): {t}\n&quot; for f, t in topics.items()))

# Check a settings file the way Muse Code&#x27;s startup does.
settings = pathlib.Path.home() / &quot;.config/muse/settings.json&quot;
if settings.exists():
    data = json.loads(settings.read_text())
    if data.get(&quot;schema_version&quot;) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(&#x27;settings.json needs &quot;schema_version&quot;: 1, or every command fails at startup&#x27;)

Done when
- AGENTS.md lists this repo&#x27;s real install, test and lint commands, and `muse init --dry-run` ran first.
- .agents/memory/MEMORY.md links every topic file, and none of them holds a secret.
- The key comes from META_API_KEY or a stored sign-in and never appears in code, logs or commits.</pre><div class="docs-prompt-foot"><span class="docs-prompt-count">3,123<!-- --> id="_R_95av5spfklb_" class="docs-toc-panel" hidden=""></div></nav></div><p class="docs-p">Set Muse Code up once for your machine and once per project, and give the agent the durable project knowledge it needs. This way, you don&#x27;t repeat yourself every session. User settings live in a JSON file. Project instructions and memory travel with the repository.</p><h2 id="settings-file" class="docs-h docs-h2">The settings file<a class="docs-anchor" href="#settings-file" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">User settings live at <code class="docs-code-inline">~/.config/muse/settings.json</code>. The file holds:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>model defaults</span></li><li><span>terminal-UI preferences, including <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/interactive#voice">voice</a>, <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/interactive#reasoning">reasoning display</a>, and the terminal theme (<code class="docs-code-inline">tui.terminal_background</code>, set with <code class="docs-code-inline">/theme</code>)</span></li><li><span>the default <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/permissions#profiles">permission profile</a> (<code class="docs-code-inline">permissions.default_profile</code>)</span></li><li><span>tool configuration, including <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/workflows#configure">workflow selection</a> and <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/session-messaging#configure">session messaging</a></span></li><li><span><a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/extending#mcp">MCP servers</a></span></li><li><span>a first-class <code class="docs-code-inline">hooks</code> block, plus a <code class="docs-code-inline">managed_hooks_path</code> pointer (see <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/extending#hooks">hooks</a>)</span></li><li><span>a <code class="docs-code-inline">runtime_capabilities</code> map that toggles capabilities such as the <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/extending#observer-agents">observer agents</a></span></li><li><span>telemetry options</span></li></ul><p class="docs-p">To delete saved sessions you haven&#x27;t opened for a while, set <code class="docs-code-inline">session_retention_days</code> to a number of days. Leave it unset to keep sessions forever. Retention works on macOS and Linux only for now. To set it for a single run, pass <code class="docs-code-inline">-c session_retention_days=N</code>.</p><div class="docs-callout docs-callout-important" role="note"><span class="docs-callout-icon"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><circle cx="10" cy="10" r="8.5" fill="currentColor"></circle><path fill="#fff" d="M9.1 5.2h1.8l-.2 6H9.3z M10 12.6a1.1 1.1 0 1 1 0 2.2 1.1 1.1 0 0 1 0-2.2z"></path></svg></span><div class="docs-callout-body"><p class="docs-callout-title">schema_version must be 1</p><p class="docs-p"><code class="docs-code-inline">settings.json</code> must set <code class="docs-code-inline">&quot;schema_version&quot;: 1</code>. A file that omits that key fails every command at startup with <code class="docs-code-inline">malformed settings file</code>. An unrecognized value fails with <code class="docs-code-inline">unsupported settings schema version</code>. A <strong>missing</strong> file is fine, because Muse Code applies defaults. Create the file only when you have something to set, and always include <code class="docs-code-inline">&quot;schema_version&quot;: 1</code>.</p></div></div><p class="docs-p">Enterprise administrators can validate a managed configuration document with <code class="docs-code-inline">muse config validate --plane &lt;defaults|policy&gt; --file &lt;path&gt;</code>, or check the active managed configuration with <code class="docs-code-inline">muse config status</code>.</p><h2 id="agents-md" class="docs-h docs-h2">Project instructions with AGENTS.md<a class="docs-anchor" href="#agents-md" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p"><code class="docs-code-inline">muse init</code> seeds your project&#x27;s agent rules. It writes a single <code class="docs-code-inline">AGENTS.md</code> into the current directory. It creates no other files, and does <strong>not</strong> change <code class="docs-code-inline">settings.json</code>:</p><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">bash</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="bash" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" style="background-color:transparent;color:var(--docs-syn-fg)" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">muse </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">init</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-comment)">            # write AGENTS.md in the current directory</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">muse </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">init</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> --dry-run</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-comment)">  # show what it would write, change nothing</span></span></code></pre></div></div><p class="docs-p">Without <code class="docs-code-inline">--force</code>, it stops if <code class="docs-code-inline">AGENTS.md</code> already exists. With <code class="docs-code-inline">--force</code>, it overwrites the file completely, so save any existing content first.</p><p class="docs-p"><strong>How Muse Code loads instruction files.</strong> From your workspace root, Muse Code walks up to the nearest <code class="docs-code-inline">.git</code> boundary. At each directory level, it checks <code class="docs-code-inline">AGENTS.md</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">CLAUDE.md</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">.agents/AGENTS.md</code>, then <code class="docs-code-inline">.claude/CLAUDE.md</code>; the first existing file in that order wins for that level. Precedence when guidance conflicts:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>Project rules win over user rules.</strong></span></li><li><span>Among project files, the <strong>deeper file wins</strong> over a shallower one.</span></li></ul><p class="docs-p">Your machine-wide user rules always load. <strong>Project rules load only after you <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/permissions#trust-scopes">trust the workspace</a>.</strong> On an untrusted checkout, Muse Code ignores project <code class="docs-code-inline">AGENTS.md</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">CLAUDE.md</code> until you trust it.</p><div class="docs-callout docs-callout-note" role="note"><span class="docs-callout-icon"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><circle cx="10" cy="10" r="8.5" fill="currentColor"></circle><path fill="#fff" d="M9.1 8.6h1.8v5.6H9.1z M10 5.3a1.1 1.1 0 1 1 0 2.2 1.1 1.1 0 0 1 0-2.2z"></path></svg></span><div class="docs-callout-body"><p class="docs-callout-title">Conservative by default</p><p class="docs-p">Muse Code is designed to follow these files, but it stays conservative about your repository by default: it won&#x27;t commit, amend, or push your work unless you ask it to in the session, it keeps scratch files outside your checkout, and it reverts incidental edits it didn&#x27;t need. The end of a task is not a request to commit.</p></div></div><h2 id="model" class="docs-h docs-h2">Select a model<a class="docs-anchor" href="#model" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">The default model is <code class="docs-code-inline">muse-spark-1.2</code>. Override it per run with <code class="docs-code-inline">--model</code>, or switch mid-session with the <code class="docs-code-inline">/models</code> slash command:</p><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">bash</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="bash" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" style="background-color:transparent;color:var(--docs-syn-fg)" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">muse </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">--model</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> muse-spark-1.2</span></span></code></pre></div></div><h2 id="reasoning-effort" class="docs-h docs-h2">Set reasoning effort<a class="docs-anchor" href="#reasoning-effort" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p"><code class="docs-code-inline">--reasoning-effort</code> trades latency for depth: <code class="docs-code-inline">none</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">minimal</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">low</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">medium</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">high</code> (default), <code class="docs-code-inline">xhigh</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">max</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">ultra</code>. Change it mid-session with <code class="docs-code-inline">/effort</code>.</p><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">bash</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="bash" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" style="background-color:transparent;color:var(--docs-syn-fg)" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">muse </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">--reasoning-effort</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> medium</span></span></code></pre></div></div><div class="docs-callout docs-callout-note" role="note"><span class="docs-callout-icon"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><circle cx="10" cy="10" r="8.5" fill="currentColor"></circle><path fill="#fff" d="M9.1 8.6h1.8v5.6H9.1z M10 5.3a1.1 1.1 0 1 1 0 2.2 1.1 1.1 0 0 1 0-2.2z"></path></svg></span><div class="docs-callout-body"><p class="docs-callout-title">Premium reasoning levels</p><p class="docs-p"><code class="docs-code-inline">xhigh</code> is an optional premium-precision level, and <code class="docs-code-inline">max</code> is the deepest reasoning level, extended reasoning beyond <code class="docs-code-inline">xhigh</code>. Muse Code offers <code class="docs-code-inline">max</code> in both Standard and Contributor mode. <code class="docs-code-inline">ultra</code> is a client-side setting that maps to each provider&#x27;s highest supported reasoning level and can make Muse Code delegate more aggressively; where a provider doesn&#x27;t support it, a request for <code class="docs-code-inline">ultra</code> runs at <code class="docs-code-inline">xhigh</code>. The Meta provider does not accept <code class="docs-code-inline">none</code>; other providers can support it.</p></div></div><h2 id="flags" class="docs-h docs-h2">Launch flags<a class="docs-anchor" href="#flags" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Muse Code has two launch surfaces with <strong>separate</strong> flag sets: the interactive TUI (<code class="docs-code-inline">muse …</code>) and headless (<code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec …</code>). Some flags exist on only one.</p><p class="docs-p">Common to both:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">--model &lt;id&gt;</code></strong>, <strong><code class="docs-code-inline">--reasoning-effort &lt;level&gt;</code></strong>: model and reasoning depth.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">--sandbox-network &lt;mode&gt;</code></strong>, <strong><code class="docs-code-inline">--disable-sandbox</code></strong>, <strong><code class="docs-code-inline">--disable-approval</code></strong>, <strong><code class="docs-code-inline">--yolo</code></strong>, <strong><code class="docs-code-inline">--trust-workspace</code></strong>: <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/permissions">permissions and sandbox</a>.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">--approval-mode &lt;mode&gt;</code></strong>, <strong><code class="docs-code-inline">--approval-judge &lt;on|off&gt;</code></strong>: tune <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/permissions#approval-modes">approvals</a>.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">--subagent-worktree-isolation</code></strong>: compatibility flag. Isolation is requested per <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/extending#multi-agent">subagent</a>; the flag does not isolate every child.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">--workspace &lt;path&gt;</code></strong>: root policy-gated workspace tools at a path.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">--no-session-log</code></strong>: don&#x27;t retain the <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/interactive#session-model">session</a> event log.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">--contributor-mode &lt;on|off&gt;</code></strong>: turn <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/subscriptions#turn-contributor-mode-on-or-off">Contributor mode</a> on or off for this run only, without changing your saved setting.</span></li></ul><p class="docs-p">Headless only (<code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec …</code>):</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">--json</code></strong> (emit JSONL events), <strong><code class="docs-code-inline">--prompt-file &lt;path&gt;</code></strong> (read the prompt from a file), <strong><code class="docs-code-inline">--max-model-steps &lt;n&gt;</code></strong> (cap the run).</span></li></ul><p class="docs-p"><code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec</code> accepts both approval flags. They configure the policy before the run starts. A headless run has no interactive UI for answering a human approval prompt, so choose a policy that can complete unattended or expect the held action to remain unresolved.</p><p class="docs-p">Both <code class="docs-code-inline">muse --no-session-log</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec --no-session-log</code> run without retained session state, which <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/interactive#session-model">disables resume and the other retained-session features</a>. Generated inline workflow scripts then use process-lifetime temporary storage, which cannot support retained recovery.</p><h2 id="transport-trace" class="docs-h docs-h2">Debug provider calls<a class="docs-anchor" href="#transport-trace" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Set <code class="docs-code-inline">MUSE_TRANSPORT_TRACE=1</code> to print raw provider request and response lines to stderr while debugging model calls. Credentials are scrubbed from the output.</p><h2 id="local-memory" class="docs-h docs-h2">Local memory<a class="docs-anchor" href="#local-memory" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Memory is Markdown you keep for the agent, so it recalls durable facts on its own. There are three scopes:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>Personal project memory</strong> (the default): stored on your machine outside the repo, private to you, scoped to this project.</span></li><li><span><strong>Project memory</strong>: committed to the repo under <code class="docs-code-inline">&lt;repo&gt;/.agents/memory/</code>, shared with everyone who clones it.</span></li><li><span><strong>Personal memory</strong>: your machine-wide notes, across all projects.</span></li></ul><p class="docs-p">Keep an index in <code class="docs-code-inline">MEMORY.md</code> and one Markdown file per topic:</p><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">text</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="text" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line">.agents/memory/</span>
<span class="line">├── MEMORY.md        # index: one line per topic file</span>
<span class="line">└── deploy.md        # a durable note the agent should know</span></code></pre></div></div><p class="docs-p">Put durable, project-specific facts here: deployment procedures, the reason a workaround exists, a service&#x27;s unusual behavior. Facts the agent could get wrong from general knowledge alone are the ones worth recording.</p><div class="docs-callout docs-callout-note" role="note"><span class="docs-callout-icon"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><circle cx="10" cy="10" r="8.5" fill="currentColor"></circle><path fill="#fff" d="M9.1 8.6h1.8v5.6H9.1z M10 5.3a1.1 1.1 0 1 1 0 2.2 1.1 1.1 0 0 1 0-2.2z"></path></svg></span><div class="docs-callout-body"><p class="docs-callout-title">Memory loads in untrusted workspaces</p><p class="docs-p">Muse Code reads committed project memory into the model&#x27;s context even in an <strong>untrusted</strong> workspace. Skills, rules, and hooks differ: they load only after you trust it. Treat a repo&#x27;s <code class="docs-code-inline">MEMORY.md</code> as a prompt-injection surface, and review it on checkouts you don&#x27;t control.</p></div></div><h2 id="recall" class="docs-h docs-h2">How the agent recalls memory<a class="docs-anchor" href="#recall" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">At the start of a session, Muse Code injects an <em>index</em> of your memory: <code class="docs-code-inline">MEMORY.md</code> plus a list of the other Markdown files (their paths, not their contents), up to 48 files. The agent reads individual files on demand, and a <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/extending#observer-agents">background observer</a> can insert a relevant note into a turn before the agent answers.</p><h2 id="next-steps" class="docs-h docs-h2">Next steps<a class="docs-anchor" href="#next-steps" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Save repeatable multi-agent orchestration as <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/workflows#save">workflows</a>.</span></li><li><span>Package reusable instructions and tools as <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/extending#skills">skills</a> the agent can load on demand.</span></li><li><span>Lock down what the agent can do in <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/permissions">permissions and safety</a>.</span></li></ul><nav class="docs-pager" aria-label="Previous and next page"><a class="docs-pager-link" rel="prev" href="/docs/muse-code/rewind"><span class="docs-pager-dir"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M14.5 6l-6 6 6 6"></path></svg>Previous</span><span class="docs-pager-title">Rewind a conversation</span></a><a class="docs-pager-link is-next" rel="next" href="/docs/muse-code/extending"><span class="docs-pager-dir">Next<svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9.5 6l6 6-6 6"></path></svg></span><span class="docs-pager-title">Extending and automating</span></a></nav><p class="docs-credit">Mirrored from<!-- --> <a href="https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/configuration" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">dev.meta.ai/docs/<!-- -->muse-code/configuration</a> <!-- -->(synced <!-- -->Oct 30, 2026<!-- -->). class="docs-prompt-preview" aria-label="Prompt preview" tabindex="0">You&#x27;re Claude Code, working in my repository.

Task
Give this repository its Muse Code project context. Run `muse init --dry-run` first; if there&#x27;s no AGENTS.md, run `muse init` and fill it with this repo&#x27;s real commands and conventions. Add .agents/memory/MEMORY.md as an index with one Markdown file per durable fact you find (deploy steps, why a workaround exists, a service&#x27;s quirks). Then show me, without writing it, a ~/.config/muse/settings.json with only what I ask for and &quot;schema_version&quot;: 1.

Read this first
Meta&#x27;s docs page &quot;Configuration and context&quot; as Markdown: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/configuration.md
It&#x27;s the source of truth for request and response shapes. The same page for people: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/configuration

Setup
- Muse Code: muse on PATH (install: curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh, or irm https://dev.meta.ai/install.ps1 | iex on Windows; check: muse --version). Its default model is muse-spark-1.2; --model picks another.
- Auth: muse reads META_API_KEY from the environment (in CI, from the secret store), else a key stored with muse auth set or a browser sign-in; not MODEL_API_KEY. Never hard-code, print or commit the key.
- Python: a plain script that runs muse through subprocess where a step needs it.

Facts to get right
- ~/.config/muse/settings.json needs &quot;schema_version&quot;: 1, or every command fails (&quot;malformed settings file&quot;; other values: &quot;unsupported settings schema version&quot;). A missing file is fine.
- Keys: permissions.default_profile, session_retention_days, show_reasoning, tui.terminal_background, agents.execution_capacity (1-64), mcp_servers, hooks, managed_hooks_path.
- From the workspace root up to .git, each level uses the first of AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .agents/AGENTS.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md. Project beats user, deeper beats shallower; project rules need a trusted workspace.
- `muse init` writes only AGENTS.md and stops if one exists (--force overwrites it).
- Memory: MEMORY.md indexes one file per topic (48 listed at most). It loads even in untrusted workspaces: no secrets or instructions in it.
- Default model muse-spark-1.2 (--model); Meta rejects --reasoning-effort none.

Starter code (Python)
import json
import pathlib

memory = pathlib.Path(&quot;.agents/memory&quot;)
memory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
topics = {&quot;deploy.md&quot;: &quot;How we ship to production and roll back&quot;}
(memory / &quot;MEMORY.md&quot;).write_text(&quot;# Memory\n&quot; + &quot;&quot;.join(f&quot;- [{f[:-3]}]({f}): {t}\n&quot; for f, t in topics.items()))

# Check a settings file the way Muse Code&#x27;s startup does.
settings = pathlib.Path.home() / &quot;.config/muse/settings.json&quot;
if settings.exists():
    data = json.loads(settings.read_text())
    if data.get(&quot;schema_version&quot;) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(&#x27;settings.json needs &quot;schema_version&quot;: 1, or every command fails at startup&#x27;)

Done when
- AGENTS.md lists this repo&#x27;s real install, test and lint commands, and `muse init --dry-run` ran first.
- .agents/memory/MEMORY.md links every topic file, and none of them holds a secret.
- The key comes from META_API_KEY or a stored sign-in and never appears in code, logs or commits.</pre><div class="docs-prompt-foot"><span class="docs-prompt-count">3,123<!-- --> characters</span><button type="button" class="docs-btn docs-btn-primary docs-btn-sm"><svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span>Copy prompt</span></button></div></div></div><button type="button" class="docs-btn docs-btn-secondary" title="Copy this page as Markdown"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span>Copy page</span></button><a class="docs-btn docs-btn-secondary" href="https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/configuration" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M14 4h6v6 M20 4l-9 9 M18 14v4.5a1.5 1.5 0 0 1-1.5 1.5h-11A1.5 1.5 0 0 1 4 18.5v-11A1.5 1.5 0 0 1 5.5 6H10"></path></svg><span>View on dev.meta.ai</span><span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a><p class="docs-rail-note">Independent concept built on Meta&#x27;s Model API.
